findings.summary: The 80px rise-and-scale entrance on the h1 and p plays at full strength for users who prefer reduced motion, because there is no prefers-reduced-motion override.
findings.fix: Add a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block that drops the translate/scale (use opacity only, or no animation).

findings.summary: The background video autoplays and loops forever with no pause control, and it ignores reduced-motion preferences.
findings.fix: Pause the video or swap in a poster when prefers-reduced-motion matches, and add a visible pause/play control.

findings.summary: The parallax scroll handler writes a transform on every scroll event, with no requestAnimationFrame throttling and no passive listener.
findings.fix: Register the listener with { passive: true } and batch the transform write in a requestAnimationFrame callback (or use a CSS scroll-driven animation).

findings.summary: The scroll-linked parallax layer keeps moving for users who prefer reduced motion.
findings.fix: Check matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') and skip the parallax transform when it matches.

findings.summary: All 24 cards get a permanent will-change on transform, opacity, top and width, and they transition top and width, which are layout properties that force reflow.
findings.fix: Animate only transform (for example translateY(-8px)) and remove the blanket will-change, or apply it only during interaction.

findings.summary: Each scroll event loops over every card, reading getBoundingClientRect and then writing style.width, which interleaves layout reads and writes and thrashes layout.
findings.fix: Use an IntersectionObserver to toggle a class, or batch reads before writes inside a passive, rAF-throttled handler, and avoid changing width.

findings.summary: The scroll progress bar is driven by changing width, which triggers layout on every scroll event.
findings.fix: Drive the bar with transform: scaleX() from a rAF-throttled passive listener or a CSS scroll() timeline.

findings.summary: The 'Learn more' links only become visible on :hover, so keyboard users tab onto links they cannot see.
findings.fix: Also reveal the link on .card:focus-within (or .more:focus-visible).

findings.summary: The reveal and lift depend on hover, so touch devices never show the links, or show them only through sticky emulated hover.
findings.fix: Show the links by default and gate the hover-only reveal behind @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine).

findings.summary: button:focus { outline: none } removes every focus indicator on buttons, so keyboard users cannot see where focus is.
findings.fix: Delete the rule, or replace it with a visible :focus-visible outline.

findings.summary: Opening the modal does not move focus into the dialog, does not trap focus, does not close on Escape, and does not return focus to the trigger on close.
findings.fix: Use a native <dialog> with showModal(), or move focus to the first field, trap Tab, handle Escape, and restore focus to #open on close.

findings.summary: If the user reopens the modal within 350ms of closing it, the pending close timeout still removes .open and hides the modal; the open and close timers are never cancelled.
findings.fix: Store the timeout IDs and clearTimeout them in openModal/closeModal, or finish the close on transitionend only if the modal is still closing.

findings.summary: The requestAnimationFrame counter loop never stops. It keeps running against a detached node after switching tabs, and each remount stacks another loop.
findings.fix: Keep the rAF ID, stop at a target value, and call cancelAnimationFrame in an unmount step that runs before panel.innerHTML is replaced.

findings.summary: The counter animates every frame regardless of prefers-reduced-motion.
findings.fix: When reduced motion is preferred, render the final value directly instead of ticking.

findings.summary: A new IntersectionObserver is created on every mount and never disconnected, so it leaks observers that hold onto removed elements.
findings.fix: Call io.unobserve on each element once it has revealed, and io.disconnect() on unmount.

findings.summary: Every mount adds another window resize listener that is never removed, so listeners pile up and keep referencing detached counters.
findings.fix: Use a named handler (or an AbortController signal) and remove it on unmount, or replace it with a CSS media query.

findings.summary: touch-action: none on html and body blocks native scrolling and pinch-zoom across the whole page on touch devices.
findings.fix: Remove it from html/body and, if needed, set touch-action: pan-y only on the carousel track.

findings.summary: The navigation dots are only visible on :hover, so touch users cannot see the controls.
findings.fix: Show the controls by default and keep the hover fade only under @media (hover: hover).

findings.summary: The dots are non-focusable divs with click handlers only, so keyboard users cannot change slides, and the controls are invisible unless hovered.
findings.fix: Use <button> elements with aria-labels, and reveal the controls on :focus-within.

findings.summary: Slides auto-advance every 3s forever, with no pause/stop control, no pause on hover or focus, and no prefers-reduced-motion check.
findings.fix: Disable autoplay when reduced motion is preferred, add a pause button, and pause on hover/focus-within.

findings.summary: The interval is not reset when the user swipes or clicks a dot, so an automatic advance can fire right after manual navigation and skip the slide the user chose.
findings.fix: Store the interval ID and clear and restart it inside go() whenever navigation is user-initiated.

findings.summary: The 0.5s sliding transform transition is not reduced or removed for users who prefer reduced motion.
findings.fix: Set transition: none (or a crossfade) on .track under @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce).

findings.summary: The touchstart listener is registered without { passive: true }, which can delay scrolling while the browser waits for the handler.
findings.fix: Pass { passive: true } to the touchstart and touchend listeners.
